newsitem.title: USA: NASD fines muni brokers on securities charges.
newsitem.headline: NASD fines muni brokers on securities charges.

text.p: The NASD said on Thursday that it fined one bond firm and three brokers for securities law violations in three cases involving the sale of municipal bonds.
The National Association of Securities Dealers said it fined Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. and one of its brokers, Robert Morris, a total of $15,000 for violating NASD fair practice rules.

NASD alleged that Morris sent "offering sheets" to other bond firms that inaccurately reported that he was a member of Dean Witter's muni bond department. NASD added that Dean Witter did not have the supervisory "checks" in place to prevent Morris' actions.
Morris, who agreed to pay $10,000, and Dean Witter, which is to pay $5,000, neither admitted or denied the charges. NASD said it considers Morris' actions "inadvertent."
A Dean Witter spokesman had no comment.

NASD also said that it fined Louisiana broker Donald LaCoste over $3 million for a variety of securities law infractions, including allegedly pocketing thousands of dollars of cash that customers gave him to buy muni bonds.
NASD said LaCoste, who also was barred from the securities business, does not have to pay the fine unless he attempts to reenter the industry.
LaCoste, who neither admitted or denied the charges, was unavailable for comment.
NASD also fined George Cole, a broker with Sentra Securities Corporation in Oklahoma City, over $28,000 for what it said were excessive price markups in unrated bonds sold to two customers.

"In four instances, Cole was involved in the sale of Texas municipal utility district bonds to two customers, at prices that ranged from 26 percent to 52 percent above the prices paid for the bonds a short time earlier," NASD said.
"In each case, there was no basis in the market for the corresponding price movement," NASD said.
Cole, who neither admitted or denied the charges, was unavailable for comment.
